title: One push, one workflow, one deploy
objective: Learners follow one git push through a GitHub Actions workflow (a fresh runner, install, build, unit tests, browser tests, a conditional deploy) and see how a failing step, a pull-request check with branch protection, and a warm cache decide whether the change reaches the server, how fast, and what stops a bad commit on the way.

recommended.why: A narrated story with a developer, a runner that starts empty and a pull request waiting for its check makes the sequence and its gates memorable for people who have never opened a workflow file.

alternative.why: A story versus a timeline chart of the same run: the chart shows where the minutes go (and what a cache saves) in a way the story cannot.

assumptions: Durations are illustrative but in a realistic range for a small Node project with Playwright tests: install 95 s cold or 14 s warm, Chromium 48 s or 4 s, build 20 s, unit tests 25 s, browser tests 140 s, deploy 35 s
The workflow is .github/workflows/test.yml with on: [push, pull_request]; the deploy step is conditional on main
One job, steps in sequence; a step that exits non-zero fails the job and every later step is skipped
The runner is a fresh Ubuntu virtual machine with a 30-minute budget; it picks up the job 15 s after the push
The dependency cache is keyed on package-lock.json and the browser cache on the Playwright version; a warm cache means both hit
A reviewer merges the pull request four minutes after the check reports; the merge commit is itself a push to main and starts a second run
Branch protection, when on, requires the workflow check to pass before the merge button works
units: real time: minutes and seconds after git push (playback runs separately, about 40 s)
checkDescription: Steps run in order and a failing step skips everything after it; deploy runs only on main (or after a merge) and only when the tests pass; with a red check, branch protection blocks the merge and without it the red pull request is merged; a warm cache makes the install and the whole run shorter.

learnerPrompts.predict: Set the unit tests to “One fails” and branch protection to “Off” before you play. Will the change reach the server? What will the pull request look like, and what will main look like afterwards?
learnerPrompts.explain: Switch the dependency cache between cold and warm. Nothing about the guarantee changed, yet the run is minutes faster. What exactly is cached, what is the cache keyed on, and why does every run still start on an empty machine?
